page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmg7a.64xlarge is an enterprise instance configured on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM virtualization. It supplies 256 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU core. The hardware profile is structured for high-capacity multi-core parallel execution without GPU hardware accelerators or attached local NVMe storage.

Network infrastructure for ecs.ebmg7a.64xlarge provides a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth capability, facilitating throughput for cluster communication and distributed services. The instance features zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and relies on external attached block storage to host file systems and persistent application data.

The 256 dedicated vCPUs provide consistent hardware allocation without shared-core contention. With 1024.0 GB of memory spread across 256 vCPUs, the hardware profile aligns with large-scale general-purpose compute needs, container orchestration control planes, microservice infrastructure, software compilation environments, and enterprise web application clusters.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmg7a.64xlarge is an enterprise-class general-purpose cloud instance built on x86_64 CPU architecture under KVM virtualization. The configuration offers 256 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1024.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU core. It provides baseline network bandwidth reaching 64 Gbps to ensure data throughput across distributed cloud deployments. This instance includes zero GPU acceleration units and no local storage volumes, relying on attached cloud storage solutions for data persistence. The dedicated vCPU model ensures dedicated hardware resource allocation free from shared multitenancy effects. The high vCPU density combined with massive system memory accommodates container orchestration backbones, high-concurrency web serving infrastructure, software build servers, and enterprise application deployments requiring consistent multi-core compute capacity.
